hint.en: Think about whether you can reuse the same pool of safety questions across several departments.

background_fact.en: Separating pools from courses allows organizations to update a central question pool once and have changes reflect everywhere.

merksatz.en: Pools are modular and attach to courses.

why.en: Pools are created independently and attached to courses as needed, and materials are linked directly from Nextcloud Files.

misconception.en: None. This correctly describes the modular architecture of the app.

why.en: The app avoids duplication by referencing pools and folders instead of locking copies into closed archives.

misconception.en: Assuming courses make isolated, static duplicates of everything you link to them.

why.en: A pool exists on its own and can serve several courses simultaneously without being tied to the lifecycle of one course.

misconception.en: Believing question pools are strictly nested sub-elements that disappear with a course.

why.en: Course owners link normal Nextcloud folders holding PDF or Markdown documents so learners can read them in the course.

misconception.en: Thinking all study texts have to be typed into single question fields.

hint.en: Consider who needs access to organizational settings versus who only needs to practice and view personal results.

background_fact.en: Instructor visibility is strictly scoped to their own courses, meaning a teacher in course A cannot inspect course B.

merksatz.en: Clear roles protect privacy and course order.

why.en: Students have dedicated learning views and cannot inspect the personal results of other participants.

misconception.en: None. This correctly outlines the student scope.

why.en: Instructors are responsible for structuring the course content, enrolling learners, and tracking cohort progress.

misconception.en: None. This matches the instructor privileges.

why.en: Administrators manage global app options, run server maintenance, and possess implicit instructor capabilities.

misconception.en: None. This correctly identifies administrator responsibilities.

why.en: Students are learners without administrative permissions; they cannot reconfigure pools or modify server settings.

misconception.en: Assuming every course member has equal administrative and editing power.

hint.en: Remember the fundamental Leitner principle for refreshing forgotten material right from the beginning.

background_fact.en: Returning missed cards to the first box prevents false confidence and guarantees that shaky knowledge is reviewed most frequently.

merksatz.en: Known advances one, missed resets to one.

why.en: This is the core mechanic of the Leitner system: gradual progression on success and an immediate return to the start on failure.

misconception.en: None. This accurately reflects how cards transition across boxes.

why.en: Cards must be reinforced across multiple intervals rather than jumping directly to mastered, and wrong answers are never deleted.

misconception.en: Believing that one single correct recall proves permanent mastery or that mistakes destroy content.

why.en: Cards advance through consecutive boxes to increase review intervals as retention deepens.

misconception.en: Thinking cards never change position in the scheduling queue.

why.en: A missed card does not gently step down one box; it returns all the way to box 1 so the concept can be rebuilt securely.

misconception.en: Assuming mistakes only cause a minor one-step demotion instead of a full reset.

hint.en: Recall the diagram showing boxes from 'new and missed' up to 'mastered'.

background_fact.en: Sebastian Leitner designed the 5-box card file in the 1970s to widen the time gap between reviews as memory strengthens.

merksatz.en: Five boxes guide cards to mastery.

hint.en: Focus on how the queue prioritizes what needs refreshing based on how well you remember it.

background_fact.en: FSRS-5 models human forgetting curves mathematically to schedule cards right before they would fade from memory.

merksatz.en: Smart Queue sorts due reviews smartly.

why.en: The Smart Queue gathers all due items and presents them systematically based on memory stability.

misconception.en: None. This correctly describes the Smart Queue function.

why.en: Cards are scheduled based on calculated due dates and memory strength rather than pure chance.

misconception.en: Believing the queue acts as an arbitrary card shuffler.

why.en: The Smart Queue prompts active recall practice; it never grants automatic completion credits.

misconception.en: Assuming the queue bypasses the practice process.

why.en: FSRS-5 maintains and updates your memory retention history instead of clearing your progress.

misconception.en: Fearing that opening the review queue wipes out existing mastery data.

hint.en: Consider what your brain must do when it reconstructs an answer compared to passive review.

background_fact.en: Cognitive research shows that retrieval practice changes memory traces so they become significantly more resistant to future forgetting.

why.en: Active recall exercises the memory pathway, which produces durable retention.

misconception.en: Assuming that effortless reading stores knowledge just as deeply as active recall.

why.en: Highlighting and passive reading remain low engagement activities that fade quickly.

misconception.en: Believing that marking text with highlighters replaces active practice.

why.en: Forgetting is a natural process that requires recurring reviews over time rather than a single effort.

misconception.en: Expecting a single successful recall session to prevent forgetting permanently.

why.en: Spaced repetition benefits any kind of knowledge, from vocabulary to organizational policies.

misconception.en: Restricting spaced practice solely to technical or mathematical subjects.

hint.en: Look for the mode designed for low pressure exploration and learning from mistakes.

background_fact.en: Receiving an explanation right after an error prevents false assumptions from consolidating in long term memory.

merksatz.en: Immediate feedback turns mistakes into insights.

why.en: Training Mode prioritizes immediate understanding through instant feedback and helpful explanations.

misconception.en: Assuming practice sessions hide your answers until the very end of the course.

why.en: Withholding feedback until the end is a hallmark of exam assessments, not training practice.

misconception.en: Confusing practice rounds with strict assessment evaluations.

why.en: Practice answers in Training Mode never issue a certificate.

misconception.en: Believing that everyday practice sessions automatically count toward certified credentials.

why.en: Training Mode allows you to study at your own comfortable pace without timer pressure.

misconception.en: Thinking that all question modes impose hard countdown clocks.

hint.en: Think about how an adaptive learning schedule benefits from knowing which cards were easy or difficult for you.

background_fact.en: Learners who accurately judge their own knowledge retention retain material longer because review sessions match their actual memory strength.

merksatz.en: Honest self-assessment optimizes your review schedule.

why.en: Honest feedback allows the schedule to calibrate repetitions precisely to your personal recall needs.

misconception.en: Thinking confidence inputs are ignored or serve merely decorative purposes.

why.en: Confidence ratings do not bypass official requirements or grant automatic passes.

misconception.en: Believing you can skip study requirements simply by claiming high confidence.

why.en: Uncertain questions need more practice, so they are kept and scheduled rather than deleted.

misconception.en: Fearing that acknowledging difficulty will make questions disappear from review.

why.en: Confidence buttons support your personal learning rhythm and are not grading criteria.

misconception.en: Treating personal self-evaluation as an audit report for supervisors.

hint.en: Think about which settings recreate the genuine experience of an evaluation exam.

background_fact.en: Practicing under simulated test constraints reduces performance anxiety and trains effective pacing under real evaluation conditions.

merksatz.en: Exams test knowledge under realistic conditions.

why.en: When the exam has a time limit, the countdown runs and the exam is submitted automatically when time runs out.

misconception.en: Assuming a timed exam keeps running after its limit.

why.en: Passing thresholds are central to testing whether minimum course requirements have been achieved.

misconception.en: Believing that exam simulations show scores without comparing them to a pass mark.

why.en: Immediate explanations belong to Training Mode; exams reserve all feedback until after submission.

misconception.en: Expecting hints and explanations in the middle of an exam.

why.en: Configurable presets let educators and learners test specific scopes and durations.

misconception.en: Assuming all test simulations must use identical fixed question counts.

hint.en: Consider whether your current goal is building foundational knowledge or testing your overall readiness under real constraints.

background_fact.en: Educational research demonstrates that low stakes practice with explanations must precede summative testing to achieve optimal learning outcomes.

merksatz.en: First train understanding, then measure success.

why.en: Training Mode creates a safe space where immediate explanations help build comprehensive understanding.

misconception.en: Thinking learners should jump into timed assessments before understanding core concepts.

why.en: Official certificates are earned through counting exams, not through exploratory training sessions.

misconception.en: Assuming Training Mode grants verified credentials for regulatory compliance.

why.en: Verifying pace and passing readiness under test conditions is the exact purpose of exam mode.

misconception.en: Using Training Mode when the goal is actually assessing exam stamina under time limits.

why.en: Mandatory recertification requires taking formal course exams rather than practice rounds.

misconception.en: Confusing everyday training practice with formal mandatory recertification attempts.

hint.en: Think about what turns an incorrect guess into a valuable micro-lesson.

background_fact.en: Learning research confirms that understanding why an intuitive choice was wrong prevents repeating the exact same error later.

merksatz.en: Feedback explains misconceptions behind every choice.

why.en: Option A correctly identifies that the feedback highlights both the right reasoning and the underlying misconceptions.

misconception.en: None. Understanding why wrong answers are wrong is essential for long-term retention.

why.en: Option B is incorrect because answers cannot be changed after submitting your decision.

misconception.en: Believing that reading explanations is a mechanism to alter past choices rather than a learning tool.

why.en: Option C is incorrect because feedback does not alter the number of cards scheduled for practice.

misconception.en: Thinking that time spent reading feedback reduces the review workload automatically.

why.en: Option D is incorrect because feedback is for personal study and triggers no instructor notifications.

misconception.en: Assuming every detailed click is logged as a reporting message for teachers.

hint.en: Consider whether a good learning hint gives away the secret or merely points you in the right direction.

background_fact.en: Cognitive science shows that partial clues stimulate active recall much better than prematurely looking up the complete solution.

merksatz.en: Hints nudge thinking without spoiling answers.

why.en: Option A accurately reflects the hint feature, which encourages independent thought through gentle guidance.

misconception.en: None. A constructive hint stimulates active memory retrieval.

why.en: Option B is incorrect because revealing the answer outright destroys the active recall process.

misconception.en: Confusing a hint with an automatic solution reveal.

why.en: Option C is incorrect because the app does not eliminate choices like a quiz show lifeline.

misconception.en: Assuming hints function like elimination lifelines in television games.

why.en: Option D is incorrect because requesting a hint is a supportive study tool and carries no penalty.

misconception.en: Fearing that asking for guidance creates a negative mark on training records.

hint.en: Look for statements emphasizing flexibility, optional sound, dual languages, and two distinct dialogue stages.

background_fact.en: Dual-coding theory demonstrates that pairing written text with spoken dialogue reinforces comprehension when learners have control over playback.

merksatz.en: Audio is optional and offers full subtitles.

why.en: Option A is correct: every spoken line has subtitles and keywords, and this question offers German and English audio.

misconception.en: None. Subtitles provide accessibility across different environments.

why.en: Option B is correct because audio is purely optional and everything functions properly without sound.

misconception.en: None. The app is fully usable without speakers or headphones.

why.en: Option C is incorrect because learners are never forced to wait through audio tracks before making choices.

misconception.en: Assuming audio elements act as forced progression timers.

why.en: Option D is correct because questions can present a small intro scene first and a debrief dialog after submission.

misconception.en: None. The structure separates the initial dilemma from the subsequent debrief.

hint.en: Think about how public digital signatures enable independent confirmation without requiring internal credentials.

background_fact.en: To protect personal privacy, the public verification page displays course details and the certificate identifier, but omits the learner's personal name.

merksatz.en: Certificates verify publicly without any login.

why.en: Option A is correct because verification relies on a public link and QR code that require no login.

misconception.en: None. The cryptographic signature provides tamper-evident validation on demand.

why.en: Option B is incorrect because external auditors do not need instructor accounts or access to private learner records.

misconception.en: Believing that certificate validation requires administrative access to the learning management system.

why.en: Option C is incorrect because verification is automated through the permanent web address rather than manual correspondence.

misconception.en: Thinking certificate checks require manual confirmation from IT personnel.

why.en: Option D is incorrect because an authentic certificate proves completion on its own without re-testing.

misconception.en: Assuming completed credentials must be demonstrated repeatedly to prove authenticity.

hint.en: Consider when the renewal window opens, whether early completion causes lost days, and which exam attempts are recognized.

background_fact.en: The renewal window opens on the day of the first reminder so learners have plenty of time to renew without risking a lapse in compliance.

merksatz.en: Early renewal preserves the original expiry date.

why.en: Option A is correct because the system sends notifications thirty days and seven days before expiry by default.

misconception.en: None. Timely notices ensure employees can plan their required refreshers.

why.en: Option B is correct because completing the exam before the deadline extends validity from the old expiration date rather than resetting it early.

misconception.en: None. Learners do not lose days by being proactive.

why.en: Option C is incorrect because recertification demands a new exam taken during the current window; prior attempts never carry over.

misconception.en: Assuming an earlier successful attempt can automatically fulfill future annual obligations.

why.en: Option D is correct because only assessments submitted after the renewal window has opened are valid for recertification.

misconception.en: None. Strictly bounding exams to the renewal timeframe protects compliance audit standards.

hint.en: Look for features designed for targeted review of due cards and personal weak spots rather than repeating everything.

background_fact.en: Spaced reviews scheduled right when forgetting begins reinforce memory far more effectively than massed rereading.

merksatz.en: Maintenance Mode keeps learned knowledge reliably fresh.

why.en: This correctly describes maintenance mode, once your instructor has switched it on, opening the review queue for due cards, and the cheat sheet focusing on your weakest areas.

misconception.en: None. This accurately reflects post-course retention features.

why.en: The app preserves your progress and schedules only due cards instead of wiping your work.

misconception.en: Believing that long-term retention requires starting the entire curriculum over from scratch.

why.en: You do not need to take full tests repeatedly; spaced reviews focus efficiently on what is due.

misconception.en: Assuming only taking entire formal exams can maintain retention.

why.en: Without deliberate review, knowledge fades over time, which is why Maintenance Mode exists.

misconception.en: Thinking that passing a topic once guarantees permanent recall.

hint.en: Consider where the app is hosted and what two separate permissions are needed before an AI service receives anything.

background_fact.en: Even when AI is configured, you can withdraw your personal consent at any time in your settings.

merksatz.en: Your learning data stays on your server.

why.en: This accurately states that data remains on your server by default and AI features require both administrator activation and individual user consent.

misconception.en: None. This correctly describes the app's privacy model.

why.en: There is no central vendor server or external benchmarking; your learning data stays on your own organisation's installation.

misconception.en: Assuming that web applications inevitably synchronize user profiles to a central vendor cloud.

why.en: Exams and certificate generation run strictly locally on your Nextcloud server without sending data outside.

misconception.en: Believing certificate verification requires external validation services.

why.en: The app never automatically transmits account passwords or email addresses to the AI service.

misconception.en: Fearing that turning on optional AI sends all confidential account credentials to the external provider.

hint.en: It combines an English word for clever with the word for a waiting line.

background_fact.en: The Smart Queue stays empty until you have started Leitner practice in at least one pool, because only then do your cards get a review schedule.

merksatz.en: The Smart Queue reviews all due cards.
